reason: The text explicitly portrays the Hebrews/Israelites as followers of Yahweh through multiple indicators: (1) God's direct command to Moses to tell the Israelites to 'serve/worship Yahweh' (וּלְכוּ עִבְדוּ אֶת־ יְהוָה); (2) The Israelites' obedience to God's instructions through Moses ('וּבְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל עָשׂוּ כִּדְבַר מֹשֶׁה'); (3) God's explicit differentiation and protection of the Israelites from the Egyptians, establishing a covenantal relationship ('לְמַעַן תֵּדְעוּן אֲשֶׁר יַפְלֶה יְהוָה בֵּין מִצְרַיִם וּבֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל'); (4) The narrative structure showing Yahweh as the directing force behind the Israelites' liberation. The text demonstrates both religious devotion and obedience to Yahweh as foundational to the Israelite identity.
